title: Stream session broker and fallback mediator for hosted edge API
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
Design and ship a lightweight "session broker" and an accompanying "fallback mediator" at the edge gateway to enable graceful active-active failover for stateful streaming sessions and request-affine tokens. The broker mediates ephemeral session ownership, checkpoints minimal streaming state (KV checkpoint/tombstones), and orchestrates controlled traffic handoffs to a fallback path without dropping in-flight streams or losing token-level progress.

Background & motivation:
Hosted API customers increasingly use long-lived streaming calls (chat, tool-calls, embeddings with large prefix) that maintain server-side KV, key-value caches, and token progress in the gateway. During region or node-level failover we must avoid: token loss, duplicated completions, sudden EOFs for streams, or systemic SLO violations. Existing active-active routing either kills streams or forces heavyweight global state sync. This ticket proposes a mediator pattern that keeps handoff lightweight, observable, and bounded in latency/cost.

Goals & non-goals:
Goals:
- Preserve user-visible token progress for >99.9% of in-flight streams during a regional drain or failover window.
- Provide deterministic circuit-breaker thresholds that trigger staged fallback with minimal client-visible disruption.
- Coordinate with existing KV-prefetch and prefix cache so rehydration of short-lived sessions is under 200ms median on failover.
- Make fallback policy pluggable (drop-in to routing stack) and controllable by SLO headroom.
Non-goals:
- Do not attempt full strong consistency across regions (no synchronous cross-region write for every token).
- Not solving heavy stateful replication for very long-running sessions (>24h); those should be surfaced as special-case enterprise flows.

Design proposal (high level):
1) Session Broker: ephemeral, per-connection controller co-located in the gateway that tracks: session_id, last_ack_token_index, small checkpoint blob (KV pointers + checksum), preferred replica region, and soft-lease expiry. The broker exposes a lightweight handshake over the streaming protocol (new header X-RW-Session-Broker) to allow the backend runtime to accept a session takeover. Brokers store minimal state in a fast local store (in-memory + local SSD snapshot) and publish short-lived leases to the telemetry plane.

2) Fallback Mediator: a separate, stateless control plane component that listens to telemetry (SLO headroom, latency percentiles, error budget burn) and decides staged fallback policies. When triggered, the mediator: (a) switches routing for new sessions, (b) instructs brokers to attempt a rendezvous checkpoint for active sessions matching filter sets, and (c) orchestrates per-session fallback behavior (rehydrate -> continue / replay -> abort-graceful).

3) Handoff protocol (session rendezvous):
- Step A: Mediator requests broker to snapshot minimal checkpoint and publish it to a local rendezvous store with a short TTL.
- Step B: Mediator instructs egress gateway to divert a small fraction of traffic (canary % per-second) to target region while maintaining sticky routing for ongoing connections until negotiation completes.
- Step C: Target region gateway fetches checkpoint (rendezvous) and attempts soft-attach by validating checksum and recovering prefix caches.
- Step D: If attach succeeds within the per-session timeout, new traffic continues on the target and old connection is gracefully drained. If not, an automatic fallback policy applies: either extend soft-lease (retry), escalate to partial-hedge (duplicate a small amount of tokens to both regions for safety), or return a well-defined stream-abort with resume token.

Circuit breakers and load-shedding integration:
- We will tie mediator decisions to SLO-driven triggers: p99 latency > SLO*1.2 for N seconds, error-rate spike, or capacity headroom < X%.
- Circuit breakers live at two levels: node-proxy (fast path) for per-process overload, and mediator-driven (global) for region-level decisions. Node-proxy breakers have fast-fail thresholds for new sessions; mediator breakers control staged diversion and per-session reattach timeouts.
- Load-shedding policy favors stopping low-value, non-persistent requests first (inference-less health checks, high-cost rerank-only calls) and preserves streaming chats with recent activity. Policy is a ranked list with cost/benefit weights supplied by Optimize heuristics.

Observability & SLO mapping:
- New metrics: session_rendezvous_latency_ms, session_attach_success_rate, session_takeover_rate, token_preservation_rate, mediator_action_rate, per-region_fallback_incidents.
- Alerts: token_preservation_rate < 99.5% over 5m, session_attach_success_rate < 95% for canary window.
- Dashboards: per-route SLO headroom, broker state distribution (leases/refresh), time-to-recovery histogram for rehydrated sessions.

Edge implementation details & trade-offs:
- Checkpoint size capped to 4KB; anything larger results in an incremental checkpoint strategy (store pointer + small digest and rely on KV-cache prefetch). This reduces cross-region transfer costs.
- Soft-lease length defaults to 45s, configurable by route. Shorter leases reduce stale ownership but increase handoff attempts.
- Trade-off: strict consistency via synchronous replication would be safer but costs >2x latency and complicates autoscale. We accept eventual rehydration with resume tokens for rare long sessions.

Testing & validation plan:
- Unit + integration tests for handshake protocol and rendezvous TTL behavior.
- End-to-end simulation using synthetic streams (varying prefix lengths, token rates) executed in CI against a multi-region staging cluster.
- Chaos engineering run: region detach during 1% production traffic with controlled canary to measure token_preservation_rate and p99 latency impact.
- Load tests to validate checkpoint throughput and rendezvous-store IOPS under burst.

Rollout plan (staged):
- Phase 0 (lab): broker + mediator in staging, wire up telemetry signals, run smoke tests (2 weeks).
- Phase 1 (canary): route 1% of traffic for low-risk routes with mediator controlling diversion; monitor attach_success and token_preservation (2 weeks).
- Phase 2 (gradual): 1% -> 10% -> 50% for broader routes (automated gating on metrics).
- Phase 3 (on-by-default): enable for all hosted API edge gateways with region policy opt-out for enterprise customers.

Acceptance criteria:
- token_preservation_rate >= 99.9% for canary routes during simulated failovers.
- session_attach_success_rate >= 97% within 200ms median rehydration; 95th < 1s.
- No more than 1% increase in median token latency for routed sessions in steady state.
- Runbook documented and SLO alerts configured.

Open questions / risks:
- Pricing impact: rendezvous transfers across regions increases egress; need BU decision on default retention policy.
- Edge storage durability: local SSD snapshot vs. remote rendezvous store availability window.
- Client compatibility: older SDKs may not support resume tokens or the new broker handshake. We need a compatibility shim and migration guidance.

updates: 2026-03-02: Initial spike and prototype wireframe completed; broker exposes header X-RW-Session-Broker and stores short checkpoint in local memstore.
2026-03-05: Prototype showed median rendezvous write 6ms, but observed tail at 450ms under I/O contention; investigating snapshot debounce and batching.
2026-03-08: Mediator stub integrated with telemetry; added SLO trigger hooks. PM review (Lena Ortiz) requested clearer fallbacks for long sessions.
2026-03-10: Design review with Security completed; agreed on checkpoint encryption-at-rest and short TTL. Assigned encryption implementation to ENG-314159.
2026-03-12: Canary gating plan accepted by SRE; scheduling canary windows and chaos run next sprint. Added compatibility shim for older SDKs to return resume token on abort.
